mainTopic: Forgiveness before יום הכפורים, the times and texts of וידוי, and the nature of the נעילה prayer
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story. רב was reading before רבי. He started over for each great scholar who entered, but not for רבי חנינא בר חמא. רבי חנינא was hurt and refused רב's apologies for thirteen years. The גמרא explains both sides: רב went beyond the law, and רבי חנינא held back on purpose because of a dream that רב would lead in בבל. A ברייתא then teaches that וידוי is said before and after the last meal on ערב יום הכפורים and in every תפילה of יום הכפורים. Several אמוראים give different texts of וידוי, and מר זוטרא teaches that 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו' is the essential part. The גמרא then asks what נעילה is, and it rejects שמואל's view in favor of רב: נעילה is a full extra עמידה. Finally, רב rules that נעילה exempts one from ערבית. A ברייתא listing a ערבית after יום הכפורים challenges that ruling, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב restarts for each scholar but not for רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רב started his reading over for רבי חייא, בר קפרא, and רבי שמעון ברבי, but not for רבי חנינא בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא came in, and רב went back to the beginning. בר קפרא came in, and he went back to the beginning. רבי שמעון the son of רבי came in, and he went back to the beginning. Then רבי חנינא בר חמא came in. רב said, 'Should I go back again so many times?' He did not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a story already in progress. רב was reading before רבי and started over every time an important scholar entered, until רבי חנינא came in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting over was a way to show respect, so the newcomer would hear the reading from the beginning. When רב skipped this honor for רבי חנינא only, it looked as if he thought רבי חנינא was less important than the others. This sets up the conflict in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he went back to the beginning

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya came in — he went back to the beginning.
phrases.notes: רבי חייא was רב's uncle and teacher.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara entered — he went back to the beginning.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי — הֲדַר לְרֵישָׁא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon son of Rebbi came — he went back to the beginning.
Rabbi Chanina bar Chama came; Rav said:
Should I go back so many times?
He did not go back.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב did not restart his reading for רבי חנינא, unlike the others.

steps.title: רבי חנינא is offended and refuses to forgive for thirteen years
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא was hurt. רב went to apologize every ערב יום הכפורים for thirteen years, and רבי חנינא would not be appeased.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא was offended. רב went to him on thirteen ערבי יום הכפורים, and he was not appeased.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב asking forgiveness every year before יום הכפורים, thirteen times, and never being forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב went on ערב יום הכפורים because one must ask forgiveness from people before יום הכפורים. The story now contains two puzzles: רב asked far more than seems necessary, and רבי חנינא refused far longer than seems proper. The next steps take up each puzzle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina was offended,
Rav went to him
on thirteen Yom Kippur eves
and he was not appeased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the result of רב not restarting for רבי חנינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב asked forgiveness thirteen times, and רבי חנינא refused each time.

steps.title: Why did רב ask more than three times?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's behavior. רבי יוסי בר חנינא taught that one should not ask forgiveness more than three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could רב act this way? But רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: Anyone who asks forgiveness from his friend should not ask him more than three times!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב. A known rule says three requests are enough, so why did he go thirteen times?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of three means that after three sincere requests, the person asking has done his duty and need not keep humbling himself. רב went far past this limit. That seems to go against the accepted rule.

keyTerms.meaning: how could he act this way?

phrases.english: And how could he act this way?
But didn't Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina say:
Anyone who requests forgiveness from his friend

phrases.aramaic: אַל יְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ יוֹתֵר מִשָּׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים!
phrases.english: should not request from him more than three times!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's rule limits requests for forgiveness to three, so רב's behavior seems to contradict it.

steps.title: רב is different
steps.stepSummary: רב was an exceptional case. He chose to act beyond what the law requires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רב in two words: רב was a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of three is worded as a limit (אל יבקש, 'should not ask'), which is why the גמרא raises the question. The answer is that רב was a special case. רב was so pious that he went לפנים משורת הדין (beyond the letter of the law), so his behavior does not contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: beyond the letter of the law (the explanation behind the answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The rule of three is worded as a limit ('should not ask more'), so the גמרא's question is real. Its answer, רב שאני, is that רב was a special case.

phrases.english: Rav is different.
phrases.notes: He was very pious and acted beyond the letter of the law.

steps.terutzMaskana: The rule sets a minimum obligation, and רב personally chose to go beyond it.

steps.title: Why did רבי חנינא refuse to forgive?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges רבי חנינא. רבא taught that whoever forgives others is forgiven for all his own sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא, how could he act this way? But רבא said: Whoever lets go of his feelings against others, Heaven lets go of all his sins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the story and asks why רבי חנינא held a grudge for so long.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's teaching shows how valuable it is to forgive. A great person like רבי חנינא would surely want that reward, so his refusing thirteen times seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: one who lets go of his feelings / does not insist on his honor

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina, how could he act this way?
But didn't Rava say:
Anyone who overlooks his own honor —
they [Heaven] overlook all his sins for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא, הֵיכִי עָבֵיד הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא teaches that forgiving others is very valuable, so refusing forgiveness thirteen times seems improper.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's dream: רב was destined to lead
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא dreamed that רב was hung on a palm tree, which means he would become a head of a yeshiva. He withheld forgiveness so that רב would go to בבל and lead there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי חנינא saw a dream about רב, that he was hung on a palm tree. There is a tradition that whoever is hung on a palm tree in a dream will become a head. He said: Learn from this that he is destined to become a leader. So I will not be appeased, so that he will go and teach Torah in בבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question on רבי חנינא. His refusal was not a grudge. It was a deliberate plan based on a dream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא understood that רב was destined to lead. If רב stayed in ארץ ישראל, he would take over רבי חנינא's position. By staying unappeased, he pushed רב to move to בבל, where רב would fulfill the dream without the two leaders clashing. So the refusal was strategic, not a failure to forgive.

keyTerms.meaning: they hung him on a palm tree

steps.whatToRemember: Both people in the story are defended. רב went beyond the law out of piety. רבי חנינא's refusal was a deliberate plan to send רב to lead in בבל, not a grudge.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא חֶלְמָא חָזֵי לֵיהּ לְרַב
phrases.english: Rather: Rabbi Chanina saw a dream about Rav
that they hung him on a palm tree,

phrases.aramaic: וּגְמִירִי דְּכֹל דְּזַקְפוּהוּ בְּדִיקְלָא — רֵישָׁא הָוֵי.
phrases.english: and there is a tradition that anyone hung on a palm tree [in a dream] — becomes a head.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ בָּעֵי לְמֶעְבַּד רְשׁוּתָא
phrases.english: He said: Learn from this that he is destined to take leadership
so [I will] not be appeased,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֵיזִיל וְלִגְמַר אוֹרָיְיתָא בְּבָבֶל.
phrases.english: so that he will go and teach Torah in Babylonia.
phrases.notes: This way רב leads in בבל without displacing רבי חנינא in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא חֶלְמָא חָזֵי לֵיהּ לְרַב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנינא simply held a grudge.
steps.terutzMaskana: He refused on purpose so that רב would move to בבל and become a leader there.

steps.title: Main time of confession and confessing before the meal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the מצוה of וידוי is at nightfall of ערב יום הכפורים. The חכמים add that one should also confess before the last meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The מצוה of וידוי is on ערב יום הכפורים as it gets dark. But the חכמים said: He should confess before he eats and drinks, in case his mind becomes confused during the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא about when to say וידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main time for וידוי is when the holy day begins at nightfall. Because a festive meal might leave a person too full or distracted to confess properly afterward, the חכמים require an earlier וידוי before eating as a safeguard.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוַת וִידּוּי עֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
phrases.english: The מצוה of confession is on Yom Kippur eve as darkness falls.
But the Sages said:
He should confess before he eats and drinks,
lest his mind become confused at the meal.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: וידוי is said at nightfall of ערב יום הכפורים, and also before the final meal as a precaution.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for saying וידוי in מנחה of ערב יום הכפורים, before the סעודה המפסקת.

steps.title: Confessing again after the meal
steps.stepSummary: Even someone who confessed before the meal confesses again after it, in case he sinned during the meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though he confessed before he ate and drank, he confesses after he eats and drinks, in case something wrong happened during the meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second וידוי after the meal, on top of the one said before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first וידוי cannot cover sins committed afterward. Since a person might have done something wrong at the meal, he confesses again at nightfall, which is also the main time for the מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה קוֹדֶם שֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁתָה —
phrases.english: And even though he confessed before he ate and drank —
he confesses after he eats and drinks,
lest some wrongdoing occurred during the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה קוֹדֶם שֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁתָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One confesses after the meal as well, because new sins may have happened.

steps.title: Confession in every prayer of יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: Even after confessing at ערבית, one confesses again at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though he confessed at ערבית, he should confess at שחרית. After שחרית, he confesses at מוסף. After מוסף, he confesses at מנחה. After מנחה, he confesses at נעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by teaching that וידוי is repeated in every one of the five תפילות of יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא follows the same pattern as before: an earlier וידוי does not exempt a later one. Each תפילה of the day gets its own וידוי, all the way through נעילה at the close of the day.

keyTerms.meaning: the closing prayer of יום הכפורים

steps.whatToRemember: וידוי is said many times: before the last meal, at nightfall, and in all five תפילות of יום הכפורים (ערבית, שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, נעילה). An earlier confession never exempts a later one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practice of saying וידוי in every תפילה of יום הכפורים.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה עַרְבִית — יִתְוַדֶּה שַׁחֲרִית.
phrases.english: And even though he confessed at the evening prayer — he should confess at the morning prayer.
[If he confessed at] the morning prayer — he should confess at the additional prayer,
[if] at the additional prayer — he should confess at the afternoon prayer,
[if] at the afternoon prayer — he should confess at the closing prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִתְוַדָּה עַרְבִית — יִתְוַדֶּה שַׁחֲרִית
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: וידוי is repeated in every תפילה of יום הכפורים through נעילה. An earlier confession never exempts a later one.

steps.title: Where in davening the confession is said
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a יחיד says וידוי after his תפילה, and the שליח ציבור says it in the middle of the תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where does one say it? An individual says it after his prayer, and the prayer leader says it in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא about וידוי keeps going. Now it tells us where in davening the וידוי belongs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An individual finishes his שמונה עשרה first and then says וידוי. The שליח ציבור places it in the middle of his repetition, inside the ברכה about the day (קדושת היום). The content is the same, but the placement differs for an individual and for the חזן.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual davening on his own
The prayer leader (חזן) who davens on behalf of the congregation
Here: the עמידה, also called שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: And where does one say it (the confession)?
An individual says it after his Amida prayer,
and the prayer leader says it in the middle.
phrases.notes: That is, inside the middle blessing about the holiness of the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about when וידוי is said, now adding where in the davening it goes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יחיד says וידוי after his עמידה. A שליח ציבור says it in the middle of his עמידה.

steps.title: What are the words of the confession?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what text one actually says for וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the actual wording of וידוי. This question sets up a list of answers in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know when and where וידוי is said, but not what to say. This question opens a list of different אמוראים, and each one gives a version or opening line.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he say? (a question asking for the wording)

phrases.english: What does one say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where וידוי is said to what words are said.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual text or opening words of the וידוי.

steps.title: Different opening lines for the confession
steps.stepSummary: רב, שמואל, לוי, רבי יוחנן, and רבי יהודה each give a different opening phrase for וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: 'You know the secrets of the world.' שמואל said: 'From the depths of the heart.' Levi said: 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying.' רבי יוחנן said: 'Master of the worlds.' רבי יהודה said: 'For our sins are too many to count, and our wrongdoings too great to number.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by listing several versions of וידוי. Each one comes from a different Sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are not really arguments about הלכה. Each Sage gives a different text or opening that he used. רב's version, 'אתה יודע רזי עולם', is the one we still say today in the וידוי of the תפילות of יום הכפורים (at נעילה a different passage takes its place).

keyTerms.meaning: From the depths of the heart

steps.confusionAlert: These Sages are not arguing about who is right. Each is offering a valid text or opening, and our מחזור actually uses several of them.

phrases.english: Rav said: 'You know the secrets of the world.'
And Shmuel said: 'From the depths of the heart.'
And Levi said: 'And in Your Torah it is written, saying.'
phrases.notes: Then one quotes the פסוק about the forgiveness of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: 'Master of the worlds.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אָמַר: ״כִּי עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ רַבּוּ מִלִּמְנוֹת
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: 'For our iniquities are too many to count
and our sins are too great to number.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי אמר' with a list of versions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Various openings: אתה יודע רזי עולם (רב), ממעמקי הלב (שמואל), ובתורתך כתוב לאמר (לוי), רבון העולמים (רבי יוחנן), כי עונותינו רבו מלמנות (רבי יהודה).

steps.title: רב המנונא's personal confession
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא gives a full, humble וידוי: I was unworthy before I was created, I am like dust, and I ask ה׳ to erase my sins with mercy and not through suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: 'My God, before I was formed I was not worthy. Now that I have been formed, it is as if I was not formed. I am dust in my life, all the more so in my death. I stand before You like a vessel full of shame and embarrassment. May it be Your will that I not sin, and what I have sinned, wipe away in Your mercy, but not through suffering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The list of versions continues with a longer one, the full וידוי text of רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This וידוי focuses on how small a person is before ה׳: unworthy before birth, and no better than dust now. It ends with two requests: to stop sinning from now on, and to have past sins wiped away through mercy rather than through painful יסורים. This text is the 'אלהי עד שלא נוצרתי' that we still say after the עמידה on יום הכפורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This exact text became part of our davening. It is said at the end of every עמידה on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
'My God, before I was formed I was unworthy.
Now that I have been formed, it is as if I had not been formed.

phrases.aramaic: עָפָר אֲנִי בְּחַיַּי, קַל וָחוֹמֶר בְּמִיתָתִי.
phrases.english: I am dust while alive, how much more so when I am dead.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ כִּכְלִי מָלֵא בּוּשָׁה וּכְלִימָּה.
phrases.english: See, I am before You like a vessel filled with shame and disgrace.
May it be Your will that I not sin,
and what I have sinned, erase in Your compassion,
but not by means of suffering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: ״אֱלֹהַי, עַד שֶׁלֹּא נוֹצַרְתִּי אֵינִי כְּדַאי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another, much longer version to the list of וידוי texts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The full 'אלהי עד שלא נוצרתי' text.

steps.title: Who used רב המנונא's confession and when
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this was the וידוי רבא said all year long, and the one רב המנונא זוטא said on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the confession of רבא all year, and of רב המנונא זוטא on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short historical note about which Sages used this וידוי and when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said this text every day of the year, not only on יום הכפורים. רב המנונא זוטא said it specifically on יום הכפורים. This shows that the text was valued both as a daily prayer and as a יום הכפורים וידוי.
steps.confusionAlert: רב המנונא זוטא ('the younger') is a different person from the רב המנונא quoted in the previous step.

phrases.english: And this is the confession of Rava all year,
and of Rav Hamnuna Zuta on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the text quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב המנונא's וידוי was used by רבא daily and by רב המנונא זוטא on יום הכפורים.

steps.title: Saying 'But we have sinned' is enough
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says the longer texts are only needed if one did not say 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו'. If he did say it, nothing more is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: We only said this when he did not say 'But we have sinned.' But if he said 'But we have sinned,' nothing more is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא sets a limit on everything listed above. Once a person says the words 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו', he has done the essential וידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The many texts above might make it sound like a long formula is required. מר זוטרא teaches that the core of וידוי is admitting 'we have sinned'. Everything else is extra that adds to the וידוי but is not required.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (limits an earlier statement)
But we have sinned (the key words of וידוי)

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said: We said this only
when he did not say: 'But we have sinned,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אָמַר: ״אֲבָל אֲנַחְנוּ חָטָאנוּ״ — תּוּ לָא צְרִיךְ.
phrases.english: but if he said: 'But we have sinned,' he needs nothing further.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the list of texts by identifying the essential minimum.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו' fulfills the essential וידוי.

steps.title: שמואל stood up at 'But we have sinned'
steps.stepSummary: בר המדודי tells how שמואל, who was sitting, stood up when the חזן reached 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו'. This shows that these words are the main part of וידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As בר המדודי said: I was standing before שמואל, and he was sitting. When the prayer leader reached and said 'But we have sinned,' he stood up. He said: Learn from this that this is the main part of the confession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to support מר זוטרא's point that 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו' is the heart of וידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל stayed seated through the rest of the חזן's וידוי and stood up only at these words. His action shows that he treated this phrase as the essential confession. בר המדודי draws that conclusion directly.

keyTerms.meaning: The main part of the confession

steps.whatToRemember: Many texts of וידוי exist, but the essential words are 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו'. מר זוטרא teaches this, and שמואל's standing up confirms it.

phrases.english: As bar Hamdudei said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, וַהֲוָה יָתֵיב,
phrases.english: I was standing before Shmuel, and he was sitting,
and when the prayer leader reached
and said: 'But we have sinned,' he stood up.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ עִיקַּר וִידּוּי הַאי הוּא.
phrases.english: He (bar Hamdudei) said: Learn from this that this is the main part of the confession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports מר זוטרא's statement with an eyewitness story.
steps.raayaObject: מר זוטרא's claim that 'אבל אנחנו חטאנו' is the core of וידוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל stood up only when the חזן said these words.

steps.title: משנה: כהנים bless four times a day on three occasions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת תענית. On three occasions (fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים), כהנים give ברכת כהנים four times in one day: at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: At three times in the year, the כהנים raise their hands four times in the day: at שחרית, at מוסף, at מנחה, and at the closing of the gates. And these are the three times: on fast days, at the מעמדות, and on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This sets up a question that will come next, about the נעילה prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ברכת כהנים is not given four times in one day. This משנה lists three special occasions when there is a fourth prayer, נעילה, and the כהנים bless at it too. The link to our sugya is נעילה, which was just mentioned as one of the times we say וידוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The closing of the gates (the נעילה prayer)
Public fast days (such as fasts for rain)
Groups of ordinary Jews who paired with the כהנים on duty and gathered to pray and read the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלשה פרקים' here means three occasions or times of year, not three chapters.

phrases.english: We learned there (in a Mishnah):
At three times in the year
the Kohanim raise their hands (to bless)
four times in the day:
at Shacharis, at Mussaf, at Mincha, and at the closing of the gates.
And these are the three times:
on fast days, at the Maamados, and on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the wording of וידוי to a new topic connected through the נעילה prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days, at מעמדות, and on יום הכפורים, כהנים bless four times a day, including at נעילה.

steps.title: What is the closing of the gates?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'נעילת שערים' from the משנה actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'closing of the gates' prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה in step 17 mentioned נעילה as a fourth time for ברכת כהנים. Now the גמרא asks what this נעילה prayer actually is, and it sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'closing of the gates' does not tell us what the prayer contains. Is it a whole new עמידה, or only a special added text? The answer will decide several הלכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Closing of the gates. The final prayer of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: What is the 'closing of the gates'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term נעילה used in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether נעילה is a full תפלה or only a special text.

steps.title: רב says a full extra prayer, שמואל says only a confession text
steps.stepSummary: רב says נעילה is a full extra עמידה. שמואל says it is only the וידוי 'מה אנו מה חיינו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is an extra תפלה. שמואל said: it is the passage 'What are we, what are our lives?'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question and they disagree. רב says נעילה is one more whole עמידה, while שמואל says it is just the confession passage 'מה אנו מה חיינו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, נעילה is a fifth complete תפלה with its own ברכות. For שמואל, there is no extra עמידה at all, only an added piece of וידוי. The rest of the sugya tests which view is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra prayer. A full additional עמידה.
'What are we, what are our lives?' The opening words of a וידוי passage.

phrases.english: Rav said:
It is an extra prayer.
And Shmuel said:
It is 'What are we, what are our lives?'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: צְלוֹתָא יַתִּירְתָּא. וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with two competing definitions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: a full extra עמידה. שמואל: only the וידוי text 'מה אנו מה חיינו'.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists five full prayers on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that at all five prayers of יום הכפורים, including נעילה, one prays seven ברכות and confesses. This challenges שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: On the night of יום הכפורים one prays seven ברכות and confesses. At שחרית, at מוסף, at מנחה, and at נעילה, one prays seven ברכות and confesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says נעילה has seven ברכות, just like the other prayers of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Seven ברכות' means a full עמידה: the first three, the middle ברכה for the day, and the last three. If נעילה has seven ברכות, it is a full תפלה, as רב said. That contradicts שמואל, who said it is only a confession text.

keyTerms.meaning: The night of יום הכפורים, meaning ערבית.
Prays seven ברכות, meaning a full holiday עמידה.

steps.confusionAlert: 'אור' here does not mean 'light'. It means the night (the evening) of יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹר יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁבַע וּמִתְוַדֶּה,
phrases.english: On the night of Yom Kippur, one prays seven blessings and confesses;
at the morning prayer, one prays seven and confesses;
at the additional prayer, one prays seven and confesses;
at the afternoon prayer, one prays seven and confesses;
at ne'ila, one prays seven and confesses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's definition using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's view that נעילה is only 'מה אנו מה חיינו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives נעילה seven ברכות, which is a full עמידה, so it cannot be only a confession text.

steps.title: An attempt to call it a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the question is an argument among תנאים and quotes a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about the וידוי at the end of יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים, as it was taught: On יום הכפורים, as darkness falls, one prays seven ברכות, confesses, and ends with וידוי. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: he prays seven, and if he wants to end with וידוי, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to defend שמואל by saying that תנאים argued about this, so שמואל could follow a different תנא. It brings a ברייתא to show that dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עם חשיכה', as darkness falls, refers to נעילה. Look closely: רבי מאיר and חכמים both say 'מתפלל שבע', so both agree that נעילה is a full seven-ברכה תפלה. They argue only about whether one must end with וידוי, so the defense does not really help שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים.
As darkness falls. Here it refers to the time of נעילה.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im,
as it was taught in a baraita:
On Yom Kippur, as darkness falls,
one prays seven blessings and confesses,
and ends with the confession;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Rabbis say: He prays seven,
and if he wishes to end with the confession, he ends that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to soften the challenge by pointing to a תנאי dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps שמואל follows a תנא who does not count נעילה as a full תפלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cited תנאים both require seven ברכות at נעילה, so the attempt fails.

steps.title: שמואל is refuted
steps.stepSummary: Since every opinion requires seven ברכות at נעילה, שמואל's view is conclusively rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of שמואל. It is indeed a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that שמואל's view is disproven. נעילה is a full תפלה, as רב said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No תנא supports the idea that נעילה is only a confession text. So the challenge from the ברייתא stands, and the formula 'תיובתא... תיובתא' closes the question.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation. The view is rejected.

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha follows רב: נעילה is a full extra עמידה with seven ברכות. It is not only the 'מה אנו מה חיינו' text.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Shmuel;
it is indeed a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Declares that the defense failed and שמואל is rejected.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: נעילה is a full extra תפלה, like רב.

steps.title: עולא בר רב leads נעילה before רבא
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר רב led נעילה. He began with 'אתה בחרתנו' and ended with 'מה אנו מה חיינו', and רבא praised him.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר רב went down to lead the prayer before רבא. He opened with 'You have chosen us' and finished with 'What are we, what are our lives?', and רבא praised him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how a חזן said נעילה in a way that רבא approved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אתה בחרתנו' is the middle ברכה of a full holiday עמידה, which matches רב's view. 'מה אנו מה חיינו', the text שמואל mentioned, still has a place as a וידוי passage at the end. So both texts are used, but inside a full תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Went down before him. He led the prayer as חזן.
'You have chosen us.' The opening of the middle ברכה of a holiday עמידה.

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא בַּר רַב נְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: Ulla bar Rav went down to lead the prayer before Rava.
He opened with 'You have chosen us'
and concluded with 'What are we, what are our lives?',
and Rava praised him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא בַּר רַב נְחֵית קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical text of נעילה after the ruling that it is a full תפלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חזן at נעילה says the full holiday תפלה and includes 'מה אנו מה חיינו' as its concluding וידוי.

steps.title: An individual says it after his prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן says that an individual says 'מה אנו' after finishing his עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא the son of רב נתן said: And an individual says it after his תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא adds a rule for someone praying alone. He says 'מה אנו מה חיינו' after his עמידה, not inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזן included the passage within the תפלה, but an individual adds it only after he finishes. This sets apart the private way of saying it from the public one.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual, praying alone (not the חזן).

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, said:
And an individual says it after his prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how an individual uses the same passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual says 'מה אנו מה חיינו' after his עמידה.

steps.title: נעילה exempts the evening prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that someone who prayed נעילה does not need to pray ערבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: the נעילה prayer exempts one from the ערבית prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a new הלכה. Davening נעילה counts in place of ערבית on מוצאי יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נעילה is said as darkness falls, close to the time of ערבית. רב says it takes the place of ערבית, and the next step explains why.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלַּת נְעִילָה פּוֹטֶרֶת אֶת שֶׁל עַרְבִית.
phrases.english: The ne'ila prayer exempts one from the evening prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: תְּפִלַּת נְעִילָה פּוֹטֶרֶת אֶת שֶׁל עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רב connected to his definition of נעילה.

steps.title: רב is consistent with his own view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב's ruling fits his view that נעילה is a full extra תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב follows his own reasoning, since he said it is an extra תפלה. Once he has prayed it, he needs nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the ruling about ערבית back to רב's definition from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since נעילה is a full עמידה said at nightfall, it can serve as the evening תפלה. According to שמואל it would be only a confession text, so it could never replace ערבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning. He is consistent.

steps.whatToRemember: רב: נעילה is a full extra תפלה, and therefore it also exempts one from ערבית.

phrases.english: Rav follows his own reasoning,
since he said: It is an extra prayer,
and since he has prayed it,
he needs no further prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב's ruling in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because נעילה is a full extra תפלה, it fulfills the evening obligation.

steps.title: How can רב say נעילה exempts ערבית if he holds ערבית is optional?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב could rule that נעילה exempts one from ערבית, since רב elsewhere rules that ערבית is only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say this? But רב said: the הלכה follows the one who says ערבית is optional!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling from Step 25 by pointing to another ruling of רב himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only need an exemption from something you are required to do. If ערבית is optional (רשות) anyway, there is nothing for נעילה to exempt you from. So רב's two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really say? (an expression of surprise that opens a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether נעילה counts as a real תפלה. The question is that the word 'exempt' only makes sense if ערבית is required in the first place.

phrases.english: And did Rav really say this?
But didn't Rav say:
The halakha follows the words of the one who says
the evening prayer is optional!
phrases.notes: This refers to the well-known dispute about whether ערבית is required (חובה) or optional (רשות).

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling from Step 25, which Step 26 had explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one who prayed נעילה is exempt from ערבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling it an exemption assumes ערבית is required. But רב rules that ערבית is optional, so there is nothing to be exempt from.

steps.title: רב was speaking according to the view that ערבית is required
steps.stepSummary: רב's exemption ruling was said according to the opinion that ערבית is required. Even by that view, נעילה takes its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the one who says ערבית is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב's exemption ruling was not his own final view about ערבית. He was explaining what follows according to the other opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב personally holds that ערבית is optional. He added that even for those who hold ערבית is required, praying נעילה covers it. So the two statements no longer clash.

phrases.english: He said it according to the words of the one who says it is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the statement to another opinion (לדברי האומר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב's exemption ruling showed his own view that ערבית is required, which would contradict his other ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב holds ערבית is optional. His exemption ruling explains that even by the view that ערבית is required, נעילה exempts it.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists a ערבית after נעילה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists all the תפלות of יום הכפורים, and it includes a ערבית after נעילה. This seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: On the night of יום הכפורים, one prays seven ברכות and confesses. At שחרית, seven and confesses. At מוסף, seven and confesses. At נעילה, one prays seven and confesses. At ערבית, one prays seven ברכות that are a short form of the שמונה עשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב by quoting a ברייתא. The challenge is still being built here and continues into the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists ערבית right after נעילה as one of the תפלות a person prays. That suggests נעילה does not exempt a person from ערבית, against רב in Step 25. The ערבית here is a weekday תפלה, so it uses a shortened version of the weekday שמונה עשרה: the first three ברכות, the last three, and one middle ברכה that sums up the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: The night of (the evening that begins the day)
A short form of the eighteen weekday ברכות

steps.confusionAlert: 'אור יום הכפורים' means the night when יום הכפורים begins, not the night after it. The ערבית listed at the end is the one after יום הכפורים is over.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
On the night of Yom Kippur
one prays seven blessings and confesses;
at the morning prayer, seven and confesses;
at the additional prayer, seven and confesses;
at Ne'ila, one prays seven and confesses;
at the evening prayer, one prays seven
as a short form of the eighteen blessings.
phrases.notes: This is the shortened weekday עמידה, with one middle ברכה summing up the weekday requests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב in Step 28, the גמרא raises a new objection to him from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one who prayed נעילה does not need to pray ערבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists ערבית after נעילה as a תפלה one prays, which implies נעילה does not exempt it.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: the ערבית after יום הכפורים is the full eighteen
steps.stepSummary: Within the ברייתא, רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says in the name of his ancestors that the ערבית after יום הכפורים is the full שמונה עשרה. His reason comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says in the name of his ancestors: one prays the full eighteen ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion about the ערבית after יום הכפורים. This sets up the next lines, where the reason and the rest of the discussion come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said this ערבית is a shortened version of the weekday עמידה. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says it must be the full eighteen ברכות. Both opinions agree that a ערבית is prayed after נעילה, so the challenge to רב still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his ancestors

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says in the name of his ancestors:
one prays the full eighteen blessings,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 29 with a disagreeing opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבית after יום הכפורים is the full eighteen ברכות, not a shortened version.
